samples.summary: The find bar's replace path writes to the Doc directly, bypassing every read-only enforcement point in the editor
samples.evidence: `handleReplace`/`handleReplaceAll` (docs-find-bar.tsx:121,130) call `state.replaceActive()`/`state.replaceAll()`, which reach `FindReplaceState.replaceMatch` (packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:78-81) and call `this.doc.deleteText(...)` / insertText straight on the `Doc`. Neither `DocsFindBar` nor `FindReplaceState` knows about `readOnly` — the component has no such prop at all — so this path bypasses both the per-handler guards in `TextEditor` and the `MUTATING_METHODS` no-op allowlist at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3939 that neutralizes every other mutating `EditorAPI` method for a viewer. The diff itself documents this bypass ('run straight against the `Doc` the find bar holds ... bypassing the editor's own mutation entry points') and adds new code to exactly these two handlers, but adds no gate. Attack: a viewer on a share link (`readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'`, shared-document.tsx:152) who reaches the replace row writes to the CRDT. I could not complete the chain to a live exploit: `findBarShowReplace` is only set by `onFindReplaceRequest`, fired from text-editor.ts:1075 which sits after the read-only early-return at text-editor.ts:894-912, so Mod+H is currently blocked and the replace row never renders for a viewer — hence low confidence. The weakness is that the only thing preventing the write is a keyboard-shortcut gate two modules away, not a check on the mutation.
searchedFor: read the MUTATING_METHODS allowlist at editor.ts:3939

samples.summary: The read-only guard is not the outermost check on the keydown path: `imageKeyHandler` runs before it, and this change makes that pre-guard handler reachable for viewers for the first time
samples.evidence: `handleKeyDown` consults `this.imageKeyHandler(e)` at text-editor.ts:865 and returns if it consumes the key; the `if (this.readOnly)` early-return is 29 lines later at :894. Before this change the handler was dead in read-only (nothing could set `selectedImage` — `handleImageMouseDown` returned at the top and no production code calls `selectImageAt`). By removing that early return (editor.ts:2558) the diff makes every branch of `imageKeyHandler` (editor.ts:2343-2429) execute for a viewer while the read-only guard is skipped. I checked each branch and found no live bypass today: Delete/Backspace route to `deleteSelectedImageInline`, which the diff correctly gates at editor.ts:2290; Cmd/Ctrl+X returns `true` without preventDefault and the native `cut` is refused by `handleCut`'s guard at text-editor.ts:1237; Escape/arrows/catch-all only move view state. The task doc under review confirms this ordering already produced one real hole ('imageKeyHandler runs before handleKeyDown's readOnly early-return, so Delete/Backspace on a click-selected image mutated a read-only document'). The residual risk is structural: any future branch added inside `imageKeyHandler` mutates a read-only document unless its author remembers to re-add the guard, and given `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` defaults to shadow mode this client flag is the effective write boundary for a viewer share link.

samples.summary: None of the three read-only gates protecting the image-resize CRDT write is pinned by a test; all three could be deleted with a green suite
samples.evidence: The diff adds `if (readOnly || !imageResizeDrag) return;` (editor.ts:2475), `if (readOnly) { render(); return; }` before the `doc.applyInlineStyle` write (editor.ts:2515), and `if (!readOnly && selectedImage)` on the drag-arming branch (editor.ts:2579). These are the only things between a viewer and a document write now that the top-level read-only return was removed from `handleImageMouseDown`. `packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts` contains no occurrence of 'image' or 'resize'; the new `copy-integrity.test.ts` drives read-only selection only through `selectImageAt`, never through a handle drag; and no test file under packages/docs/test references `imageResizeDrag`, `handleImageResize*` or `hitTestImageHandle` at the editor level. The task doc under review admits this ('none of the three is pinned by a test ... removing any one of them would not turn a test red'). Because the CI lanes prove only that the suite is green, a regression that re-opens viewer resize would ship silently.
searchedFor: grep imageResize|hitTestImageHandle|handleImageResize|resize across packages/docs/test (6 files, none an editor-level read-only resize test)
grep readOnly in packages/docs/test/view/copy-integrity.test.ts via the diff (read-only cases use selectImageAt + keydown/clipboard only)

samples.summary: Arming the read-only link-follow from the capture-phase image branch can navigate on a press the user did not finish as a link click, and can leave a stale pending href
samples.evidence: `handleImageMouseDown` calls `textEditorRef?.recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse(e)` (editor.ts:2614) and then `stopImmediatePropagation()`, so `TextEditor.handleMouseDown` never runs for this press — none of its bookkeeping (isMouseDown, drag-selection state) is established. `handleMouseUp` (text-editor.ts:2005-2016) then opens `readOnlyPendingLinkHref` whenever the selection is collapsed, and `selectImageInline` has just set the range to null (editor.ts:1256), so the range is unconditionally collapsed: pressing on a hyperlinked image and releasing anywhere else in the container still navigates, and a press that ends outside the container never reaches the container-scoped mouseup, leaving the href armed to be consumed by a later, unrelated click. Impact is bounded — `isSafeUrl` restricts the destination to http/https/mailto/tel and `window.open` uses `noopener,noreferrer` — so this is unexpected navigation to a document-author-controlled URL rather than script execution. Low confidence because the stale-href variant also exists on the pre-existing text-link path; the diff adds a second arming site that structurally cannot pair with the mousedown-side bookkeeping.

samples.summary: Server-side write authorization for viewer share links is shadow-mode by default, so the client `readOnly` flag this change widens is the only effective write boundary
samples.evidence: `YorkieAuthController` computes the per-document read/write decision but returns ALLOW whenever `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE !== 'true'` (constructor at :86-88, shadow branch at :97-105); packages/backend/README.md:111 documents `false` as the default. `readOnly` in the frontend is derived purely client-side (`packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:152`, `readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'`) and passed into `initialize()`. In a default deployment, therefore, any client-side read-only gap in the docs editor is a real write for an anonymous viewer, not a UX inconsistency. This is pre-existing and outside the diff, but it is the assumption the change under review leans on: the diff deliberately opens `handleImageMouseDown`, the textarea focus and the key/clipboard handlers to viewers and compensates entirely with client-side `readOnly` checks (the design doc it adds says so explicitly at docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:292). Reported so the widened surface is weighed against the enforcement posture rather than assumed to be backstopped by the server.

verdict.reason: The described code exists (docs-find-bar.tsx:121-137 -> find-replace.ts:78-87 writes straight to the Doc, uncovered by the MUTATING_METHODS allowlist at editor.ts:3939-3957), but it is unreachable for a read-only viewer. The replace handlers are called only from the replace row, which renders only when `showReplace` is true (docs-find-bar.tsx:277, 288-301, 161-169). `findBarShowReplace` has exactly one `true` setter in the repo, docs-view.tsx:430-433 inside `editor.onFindReplaceRequest`, which is fired from the single site text-editor.ts:1072-1077 — placed after the read-only early return at text-editor.ts:894-912, where any non-navigation key (including `h`) returns after handling only Mod+A and Mod+F. `readOnly` is correctly threaded to that guard (docs-view.tsx:327 -> editor.ts:2253 -> text-editor.ts:538-540). No toolbar, menu, or mobile entry point sets showReplace (grep across packages/frontend/src found none; DocsFindBar is rendered only at docs-view.tsx:599-606). Server-side, viewer share tokens are denied write verbs at yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200, and editor.ts:3936-3938 documents client read-only as a convenience with the store/server as the authoritative boundary. Real hardening gap, but no attacker-reachable bypass — not a blocking authorization defect.

finding.evidence: `YorkieAuthController` computes the per-document read/write decision but returns ALLOW whenever `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE !== 'true'` (constructor at :86-88, shadow branch at :97-105); packages/backend/README.md:111 documents `false` as the default. `readOnly` in the frontend is derived purely client-side (`packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:152`, `readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'`) and passed into `initialize()`. In a default deployment, therefore, any client-side read-only gap in the docs editor is a real write for an anonymous viewer, not a UX inconsistency. This is pre-existing and outside the diff, but it is the assumption the change under review leans on: the diff deliberately opens `handleImageMouseDown`, the textarea focus and the key/clipboard handlers to viewers and compensates entirely with client-side `readOnly` checks (the design doc it adds says so explicitly at docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:292). verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repo. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-87 gates enforcement on YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true', and :97-105 discards any computed deny in shadow mode, overwriting the response with status 200 / allowed:true. The viewer-write decision that gets discarded is at :200 (needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true). packages/backend/README.md:111-114 documents false as the default, and README:186-187 plus docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:200-205 confirm shadow is the shipped default stage. The frontend flag is purely client-derived at shared-document.tsx:152 (readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'). I searched for an alternative server-side gate and found none: the minted share token (auth.service.ts:35-37, 74-79) carries only the opaque shareToken with no write scoping, and no deployment config in the repo sets ENFORCE=true (only the unit-test mock at yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts:55). This is a real access-control weakness in the security lane — a permission gate that is computed but not on the enforced path, leaving a client-side flag as the only write boundary for anonymous viewer links. Pre-existing/out-of-diff status does not refute it, and no named refutation ground applies.

mergedFrom.summary: `handleImageHover` is not read-only gated, so a viewer gets resize cursors over handles the overlay does not draw and the editor refuses — contradicting the branch's own claim that the hover cursor stays gated

finding.summary: Image-resize commit writes to the document with no `readOnly` check of its own; the change moved the only read-only gate from the top of `handleImageMouseDown` into one branch
finding.evidence: Before this change `handleImageMouseDown` began with `if (readOnly) return;`. The diff deletes that and re-gates only the handle branch (`if (!readOnly && selectedImage)`, editor.ts:2559). The mutation itself — `handleImageResizeMouseUp` → `docStore.snapshot(); doc.applyInlineStyle({...}, { image: merged })` (editor.ts:2512-2520) — carries no `readOnly` check, and neither does `handleImageResizeMouseMove`. I traced every assignment to `imageResizeDrag` (grep `imageResizeDrag = ` → editor.ts:2497, 2567, 3856) and found no second entry point, so there is no live bypass today: the single branch condition is the whole enforcement. That makes it a one-line-deep gate protecting a CRDT write, and the branch's own task note concedes it is unpinned (`docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md`, "Known coverage gap": "That gate is the only thing stopping a viewer from resizing — the resize commit carries no readOnly check of its own... removing it would not turn any test red"). Impact if it regresses is a real unauthorized write, not merely cosmetic: the server-side Yorkie auth webhook that would otherwise deny a viewer's `rw` push runs in shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105, which returns allow on every deny while unenforced), so for an anonymous `role: 'viewer'` share link the client-side `readOnly` flag is currently the effective write boundary. Suggest an `if (readOnly) return;` at the top of `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (and/or in the commit helper) so the write site is self-guarding rather than trusting one caller.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the image-resize commit path has no readOnly check of its own and that the only gate is the branch condition in handleImageMouseDown. Both write-path handlers in the current tree self-guard: handleImageResizeMouseUp has `if (readOnly) { render(); return; }` at editor.ts:2515-2518, placed after listener teardown and before the mutation at editor.ts:2532-2540 (docStore.snapshot() / doc.applyInlineStyle), with a comment (2511-2514) stating it is gated there rather than trusting the caller; handleImageResizeMouseMove has `if (readOnly || !imageResizeDrag) return;` at editor.ts:2475 with a comment (2471-2474) saying it carries its own gate. The arming branch at editor.ts:2579 (`if (!readOnly && selectedImage)`) is therefore one of three independent checks, not the sole enforcement. The exact remediation the finding requests is already implemented. The reviewer's cited line range (2463-2524) is offset from the actual file, which likely explains the miss. Confirmed there is no other assignment to imageResizeDrag besides the arming site (2587) and the reset (3892).
